issues.reason: Categorical statements routes 'X is a(n) ADJ N' to ordinary copular atoms and Compound concepts splits a descriptive adjective from its head noun ('a dented pail' = two atoms), so (ConditionalProperty man sight sk_kitchen_1) is the surface predication rendered faithfully — 'an uncommon sight' entails 'a sight', the atom is true and well-typed, and the scene-vs-referent objection is graceful improvisation in acknowledged gap territory.

(Degree man uncommon quite) sits outside the ConditionalProperty restriction and so states at top level that the kind 'man' is quite uncommon simpliciter, which is false and is exactly the 'never strip the restriction' failure Conditional properties warns against.

gaps_confirmed: evaluative predicate nominals whose subject denotes a scene rather than a member of the predicate class ('X is a rare/common sight')
a restrictive locative PP inside the SUBJECT NP ('a man in the kitchen') as opposed to one restricting the kind-level claim — reusing the ConditionalProperty condition slot silently re-scopes it
new_gaps: no licensed carrier for an intensifier once a property has been restricted into a ConditionalProperty — Degree has only (Degree X scale level) and no condition slot, so 'quite' cannot be recorded under the restriction
repair_summary: Removed (Degree man uncommon quite), the only atom asserting an unrestricted degree of uncommonness of 'man'; no licensed restricted-degree form exists to replace it.
notes: The intensifier 'quite' is therefore lost rather than re-encoded, per the rule that removing a false atom is a fix while replacing it with an invention is not. The two ConditionalProperty atoms and the typed kitchen witness are left untouched.
